answer: Time-locked stake bonding curbs Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock collateral in an escrow contract with an unbonding delay before bidding on island mapping, fable translation, or prism optics jobs. Because each key needs a distinct bond subject to slashing for equivocation or failed audits, attackers incur linear capital lockup and opportunity costs per clone. Still, wealthy actors can fund many identities whenever expected payouts exceed capital costs.
